title: Teespring: 8.2M accounts breached
summary: In April 2020, the custom printed apparel website Teespring suffered a data breach that exposed 8.2 million customer records. The data included email addresses, names, geographic locations and social media IDs.

title: yotepresto.com: 1.4M accounts breached
summary: In June 2020, the Mexican lending platform yotepresto.com suffered a data breach. Over 1.4 million customers were impacted by the breach which disclosed email and IP addresses, usernames and passwords stored as bcrypt hashes. The data was provided to HIBP by dehashed.com.

title: University of California: 547.4K accounts breached
summary: In December 2020, the University of California suffered a data breach due to vulnerability in in a third-party provider, Accellion. The breach exposed extensive personal data on both students and staff including 547 thousand unique email addresses, names, dates of birth, genders, social security num

title: Fotolog: 16.7M accounts breached
summary: In December 2018, the photo sharing social network Fotolog suffered a data breach that exposed 16.7 million unique email addresses. The data also included usernames and unsalted SHA-256 password hashes. The site was dissolved the following year and repurposed as a news website based in Brcko, Bosnia

title: Nameless Malware: 1.1M accounts breached
summary: In January 2021, NordLocker provided HIBP 1.1 million email addresses collected by nameless malware. The malware campaign ran between 2018 and 2020 and infected 3.25 million computers, stealing files, credentials and taking screenshots and photos using the computer's webcam. title: Domino's India: 22.5M accounts breached
summary: In April 2021, 13TB of compromised Domino's India appeared for sale on a hacking forum after which the company acknowledged a major data breach they dated back to March. The compromised data included 22.5 million unique email addresses, names, phone numbers, order histories and physical addresses.

title: JD: 77.4M accounts breached
summary: In 2013 (exact date unknown), the Chinese e-commerce service JD suffered a data breach that exposed 13GB of data containing 77 million unique email addresses. The data also included usernames, phone numbers and passwords stored as SHA-1 hashes.
